svg.title: Dense vs. sparse embedding of one item
svg.desc: A dense embedding fills all 768 of its dimensions with non-zero values. A sparse code spreads the item over 4096 dimensions but an encoder keeps only the k = 64 strongest (top-k) and zeroes the rest, so it is stored as 64 index-value pairs, can be looked up exactly in an inverted index, and its active dimensions tend to mean something, e.g. detective fiction, while dense dimension 347 means nothing on its own.
svg.text: Dense fills every slot; sparse switches on a few
One item’s embedding · each square = one dimension
Keep the k strongest: less to store, exact lookup, readable dims.
